newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Lauda Air posts 12.9 pct 1996 net rise.
newsitem.headline: Lauda Air posts 12.9 pct 1996 net rise.

text.p: Austrian carrier Lauda Air said on Thursday net profit for the year to October 31, 1996 rose 12.9 percent to 53.1 million schillings, compared with 47 million the previous year.
Sales revenues from flights rose 29.3 percent to 3.457 billion schillings, against 2.673 billion a year ago and pre-tax profit was up 40 percent at 66.5 million.

The company said in a statement that it would pay the same dividend as it has for the past two years, which amounts to four schillings on common stock, while holders of participation certificates receive eight schillings.

The airline's founder and chief executive, ex-racing driver Niki Lauda, said in October the dividend for 1995/1996 was unchanged and forecast a net result of between 40 to 50 million schillings. The results follow hot on the heels of an announcement by rival Austrian Airlines on Wednesday that it would acquire a 36 percent stake in Lauda.

The news came shortly after German flag carrier Deutsche Lufthansa said it would cut its stake in Lauda Air to 20 percent from 39.7 percent and sell its share package to Austrian Air. Niki Lauda would retain 30 percent of the voting rights, Austrian Air said.
